articles.title: OCR returned 40 text boxes for a 34-cell table: text boxes are not cells
articles.excerpt: The easy assumption is that OCR on a picture of a table returns a list of cells, so a spreadsheet is one split on Tab away, or on whitespace if the Tabs look odd. In this test the counts did not suppo…
articles.body: The easy assumption is that OCR on a picture of a table returns a list of cells, so a spreadsheet is one split on Tab away, or on whitespace if the Tabs look odd. In this test the counts did not support it. A work-order table with 34 filled cells came back as 40 text boxes. A price list with 63 cells came back as 58. Neither equals the number of cells, and they miss in opposite directions. The text came from ImgIng https://imging.ai/ on its default tier, in a desktop browser on an Apple-silicon Mac, with both the TXT and the JSON exported. The seven sample tables are self-made with made-up data, clean and not tilted, one per kind, each recognised once. "Pasting" below means a small program that splits each line on Tab and fills a grid, not a real spreadsheet app.
articles.author: yue xing

articles.title: Table OCR to Excel: wrapped cells had no cheap fix, 11 of 34 still wrong on an unruled sample
articles.excerpt: Picture a freelance request: the client has a work-order table, but what arrives is a screenshot, and the job is to get it into a spreadsheet. OCR reads the characters fine and the columns break. On a…
articles.body: Picture a freelance request: the client has a work-order table, but what arrives is a screenshot, and the job is to get it into a spreadsheet. OCR reads the characters fine and the columns break. On a self-made 7 × 5 sample with six two-line cells, rebuilding the grid from box coordinates left 4 of 34 cells wrong when the table had ruling lines and 11 of 34 when it did not. Cutting along the ruling lines got all 34 right, which needs the lines to be there. What was tested The sample is a fictional work-order table drawn for this test, in Chinese: 7 rows, 5 columns, 34 non-empty cells, six of them holding two lines of text. There are two renderings of the same data, one with ruling lines and one without, both clean and unskewed, so everything below is about these two images.

articles.title: A trash cleanup that deleted records a day early, and how I tested it in 2 minutes
articles.excerpt: Twenty, the open-source CRM, keeps deleted records in the trash for 14 days before deleting them for good. At least, that's what it says. A record deleted at 23:50 was actually gone after 13 days and…
articles.body: Twenty, the open-source CRM, keeps deleted records in the trash for 14 days before deleting them for good. At least, that's what it says. A record deleted at 23:50 was actually gone after 13 days and 20 minutes. With retention set to 1 day, a record deleted just before midnight UTC disappeared 11 minutes later. The code looked reasonable: private calculateCutoffDate(trashRetentionDays: number): Date { const cutoffDate = new Date(); cutoffDate.setUTCHours(0, 0, 0, 0); cutoffDate.setDate(cutoffDate.getDate() - trashRetentionDays + 1); return cutoffDate; } A nightly job at 00:10 deletes everything with deletedAt < cutoff. The + 1 moves the cutoff forward a whole day, so anything deleted during day 0 is removed at 00:10 on day 14, whatever time it was deleted.

articles.title: Build Better Engineers, Not Just Better Software
articles.excerpt: I once worked on a coding project where I was effectively the junior. I had picked up a fix, worked through it and opened a pull request. I was pumped about it. I knew I still had a lot to learn, and…
articles.body: I once worked on a coding project where I was effectively the junior. I had picked up a fix, worked through it and opened a pull request. I was pumped about it. I knew I still had a lot to learn, and I was looking forward to the review, because that was where the learning would happen. Later, I noticed the pull request had been taken over. Someone else had made their own fixes to it and merged it. No review comments, no explanation. The task was done, and I was left looking at a merged pull request that no longer really felt like mine. I was kind of mad. I still did not know what had been wrong with my version, or why the changes were needed. I did not get the learning I had been hoping for, and I did not get the simple good feeling of finishing something I had started.

articles.title: Tuwunel vs Synapse: CPU, RAM and Disk Costs of a Self-Hosted Matrix Alternative to Slack or Discord in Docker
articles.excerpt: For most small groups leaving Slack or Discord, Tuwunel is the better starting point. It is one Rust binary with an embedded RocksDB database, so you run one container, not a homeserver plus PostgreSQ…
articles.body: For most small groups leaving Slack or Discord, Tuwunel is the better starting point. It is one Rust binary with an embedded RocksDB database, so you run one container, not a homeserver plus PostgreSQL plus Redis and workers. Synapse is still the safer choice once you need enterprise single sign-on, a mature admin API or room to grow past a few hundred active users. The hardware gap between the two is real, but voice and video calls, media storage and joining large federated rooms affect your bill more than the server you pick. TL;DR: which Matrix server fits you A family or friend group of 5 to 15 moving off Discord : run Tuwunel, because one container on a mini PC or a small VPS is enough and there is no database to look after.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 20, 1998:  Russia launches 1st module of International Space Station as construction begins on the largest human-built structure in orbit
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. It was just one piece, but the foundation of something much larger.
articles.body: On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station.

articles.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
articles.excerpt: Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing the lunar environment may suffer irreversible damage if things move too fast.
articles.body: Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment.
